record.title: Mae Sot–Myawaddy Bridge I restricts entry during March 2023 fighting
record.region: East and Southeast Asia and Oceania
record.scope: Thai–Myanmar Friendship Bridge I, Ban Rim Moei.
record.direction: Thailand to Myanmar for the stated visitor category.
record.movement: Thai and other foreign visitors entering Myanmar through Bridge I.
record.exceptions: Myanmar shoppers already in Thailand could return; this was not a ban on every person in both directions.
record.imposing_authority: Myawaddy authorities, coordinated with Thai immigration at Mae Sot.
record.enforcement: Immigration stopped planned visitor trips; next-day reports described the checkpoint physically reopened.
record.consequences: Visitor trips cancelled; subsequent travel remained deterred by insecurity.
record.relationship: Separate from EA007, which ended with January 2023 COVID reopening. Bridge II freight and inland highway interruption are not assigned the Bridge I endpoint.
record.status_observation: Evidence dated in the cited reports; no present status inferred.
record.official_rationale: Protect crossers during fighting in Myawaddy, according to authorities.
record.context: Armed opposition attacked the trade-zone area. A separate cargo stoppage also occurred at Bridge II.
record.uncertainty: Reopening on 26 March is reported, but tourists did not resume crossing that day. A 28 March article repeats the 25 March closure narrative without a distinct second onset. Continued cargo and inland-road restrictions are excluded.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible for a single continuous-duration calculation; see movement scope, phases and uncertainty. Reported closure/reopening dates only; no elapsed operational duration calculated.
